title: Arc Raiders 2.0 is here, and you can finally turn those lights on your backpack off
summary: Just because I'm sneaking around doesn't mean I don't want to look my best.
body: I remember being a kid and wishing I had shoes that lit up. I know now that I was a fool. If I festooned myself with garish lights, how would I scavenge for supplies in a frozen wasteland without being spotted by strangers who may or may not kill me before I can use my grappling hook to get away? This isn't a real problem I have, nor is it a real problem Arc Raiders players will have anymore, since your backpack now has an emissive toggle. That's one of many little overhauls that arrived in Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter Thursday, and you can read all about the rest in the 2.0 patch notes . If you've not been tuned into the extraction world as of late, you did indeed read that right: Arc Raiders has gotten a big shakeup with the Frozen Trails update , which comes bearing snowy mountains and grappling hooks. But that's not what's exciting about patch notes—the best part of combing through each little bullet point is seeing all those long-awaited bug fixes and little quality-of-life changes like the aforementioned emissive toggle for backpacks. That and tidbits like "added mouth animation for when players are talking in proximity chat," which I can only hope looks as sil…

summary: The actor and YouTuber guides us through the games on his PC.
body: Disk Cleanup (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?" SungWon Cho got into PC gaming through the children's adventure games developed by Humongous Entertainment. "Games like Freddi Fish, Spy Fox, those really stuck with me," says the YouTuber and actor. "I remember playing those at a pretty young age and just being obsessed with the characters, the dialogue. I don't really play adventure games now, but I did then." Cho gained a following on YouTube through his viral comedy skits such as " a villain who unintentionally always does helpful things " and when you have a really good turn in a card game , building a channel that today has almost four million subscribers. Alongside producing his own videos, Cho has become a prominent voice in gaming and animation, with roles that include Ratatoskr in God of War: Ragnarok , Abby Saja in the Netflix movie KPop Demon Hunters, and most recently, the narrator in Paramount's Golden Axe animated series. title: The developer of an AI-powered driving instruction simulator is spending $1,000 per month just to keep its demo running
summary: Teach My Little Sister How to Drive centres around a costly chatbot.
body: One of the many ways AI will (supposedly) revolutionise the games industry in facilitating highly reactive NPCs via LLM-powered chatbots. Yet so far, only a handful of games like Where Winds Meet have attempted to implement the tech, and the results have been less than spectacular. But there might also be another reason why relatively few games feature LLM-powered NPCs, which is that powering such chatbots can be costly, as recently demonstrated by the developers of an upcoming driving instructor simulator As reported by FRVR (via Kotaku ) Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is a comic simulation game in which you coach your virtual sibling on driving technique from the comfort of the passenger seat. The twist is that behind your sister's dinner-plate eyes is an LLM chatbot (currently powered by an OpenAI model, though the developers intend to use Gemini for the final release) In the role of instructor, players can both converse with the chatbot and issue vocal instructions such as "turn left here", to which the bot will respond accordingly. title: Squadron 42 has a Steam page
summary: Star Citizen's singleplayer mode gets a new trailer and more signs of life.
body: In August, game director Chris Roberts said that Star Citizen's singleplayer component, Squadron 42, was being delayed out of 2026 to avoid clashing with Grand Theft Auto 6 . There was a certain amount of skepticism about the reason for the delay, thanks in part to a recent Star Citizen livestream being declared a disaster , but also because, well. These games have had so many release dates the changes have their own wiki page . There's something concrete about having Squadron 42 getting a Steam page though, with system requirements and everything. Those system requirements are charmingly old-fashioned, with no mention of ray tracing-capable GPUs or DirectX 12. Although the install size of 150GB is still pretty hefty. ( Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is apparently going to be 200GB , oof.) There's also a new trailer, which leans heavily on the oorah stuff that's always a bit of a turn-off in military science-fiction. Privateer was my favorite Wing Commander game because it left out all the Top Gun nonsense, but of course it's front-and-center in Squadron 42. So too are the celebrity actors, with appearances by Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Rhona Mitra, that guy who played the Onion Knight…

title: WoW: Forever, by casting off modern convenience, has horseshoed back around to being casual friendly again
summary: No Season-ing.
body: Terminally Online (Image credit: Future) This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice. World of Warcraft: Forever seems, at first blush, like an antidote to the idea of a modern MMO. I see it in the (naturally, traditionally) insufferable trade chat as I potter about on my fury warrior—people turning up their noses at the idea of retail players. Cushioned as they are in their soft little bubbles, ptooie! But as someone with a 9-5 job and other MMOs I play, I wouldn't particularly describe myself as a "hardcore" WoW player. Competent, sure. I've cleared high-end content in other games (like a Savage tier in FF14). I know how to push buttons and avoid mechanics—and I also like hard games in general . But I'm definitely not on that grindset, particularly not in a beta. title: Triple-A Minesweeper is a gleeful send-up of blockbuster gaming's worst habits, from yellow paint to characters who talk too much
summary: "Oof, a mine!"
body: In recent years, triple-A games have often been criticised for overly excessive handholding, overcompensating for a dread fear that the player might become stuck. This has manifested in numerous ways like Atreus' heavy-handed puzzle hints in God of War: Ragnarok , yellow paint splashed on every other ledge of Stellar Blade , and most recently, Marvel's Wolverine essentially playing itself for entire portions of the game. I'm not here to weigh in on that debate. Instead, I'm simply going to point you to Triple-A Minesweeper , a delightful spoof game created by developer Mike Lacher, which expertly skewers some of blockbuster gaming's most egregious habits. Now, before I describe the experience of playing Triple-A Minesweeper, I strongly suggest that you go and play it . It only takes about five minutes, so in explaining it I will probably tell you about most of the game. It should also give you a giggle, perhaps several, even! title: 'If you're skilful enough, you can chop the head off a monster, kick it midair, and then kill another monster with it': Consider me sold on this indie first-person ARPG
summary: Heathen puts a new perspective on Diablo, and it looks brilliant.
body: Certain ideas that crop up every so often in games will always grab my attention. One of them is letting players defeat enemies with bits of other enemies. As such, my interest in Heathen—an upcoming indie dungeon crawler—went from 'mildly curious' to 'smashing the wishlist button' when its most recent trailer revealed you can beat your foes by volleying other enemy heads at them. Developed by solo developer Christoper Yabsley, Heathen takes the frantic monster bashing and loot hoarding of Diablo and reworks it for a first-person perspective. Set in the fantasy town of Saltgrave, it sees your character seeking fortune and glory in the vast subterranean labyrinth beneath the town, encountering an "ancient horror" in the process in what the Steam page describes as a "descent into madness." The chief addition that the trailer explores is a new enemy dismemberment system added by Yabsley, which he says has "done a lot for making swords and axes feel really good". As a longtime fan of first-person melee games like Dark Messiah of Might and Magic and Warhammer: Vermintide 2 (the latter of which is an influence on Heathen's combat), I'm highly impressed by how slick and tactile Heathen's…

body: We've been running a knockout tournament that puts graphical effects in games against one another in a fierce battle of public opinion. title: When the weather turns foul in Arc Raiders' Pendola Pass, take a trip to a Storm Hut—they're some of the best loot spots I've found
summary: Especially if you're looking for vague outpost crafting items like the Epoxy Bucket and Insulation Roll.
body: Arc Raiders ' Pendola Pass is packed to the gills with loot. No matter where you search, you're likely to come away with some rare items, whether you're smashing open iced up doors to get into sealed rooms, or climbing into hard-to-access spots with the Grappling Hook and yoinking everything not nailed down. But some of the best loot spots I've found are the Storm Huts. Pendola Pass has a special weather condition called Flash Freeze where a snow storm randomly moves in and you start taking damage after a while, similar to the previous Cold Snap map condition. You'll also hear an emergency broadcast over loudspeakers explaining that the temperature outside is deadly, and special shelters are being opened up. Storm Huts only open and appear as map icons when the Flash Freeze hits Embark Studios But they contain a lot of loot, including new crafting materials Embark Studios These are the Storm Huts and they won't appear on your map until the Flash Freeze occurs. Even if you find one, the door will be sealed, so they're only accessible when the cold hits. You might be thinking, well, I can shelter in any building, right? title: How to complete Tracks of the Beast in Arc Raiders
summary: Find the destroyed station then ping a Bully and Skulker.
body: Head to the north of Pendola Pass then go south along the tracks to Almatera Station (Image credit: Embark Studios) Key deets ⚡ Head to the northern tracks in north Pendola Pass. ⚡ Follow them south to Almatera Station. ⚡ Keep your eyes peeled for a Bully and Skulker to ping along the way. The Tracks of the Beast quest in Arc Raiders involves travelling along some train tracks and pinging the new Pendola Pass enemies, the Bully and the Skulker. First off, head to the northern tracks area in the north of the new map—this area encompasses the entire north, so it's easy to complete. After that, head to Almaterra Station to the south, preferably following the train tracks, since there are often Bully and Skulker enemies in this area for the next step. Ping a Bully The Bully is hard to miss due to the loud distinctive sound it makes when it aggros (Image credit: Embark Studios) The challenging part of Tracks of the Beast is you have to do all of the steps in a single round. The Bully is the first enemy you have to ping and it's kind of like a big arc horse-dog robot: There's usually a Bully in Old Town in the southwest of the map. title: How to complete To the Skies in Arc Raiders
summary: Help Apollo repair the Gondola Prototype.
body: Your first step is scanning a crashed Arc Probe and Courier (Image credit: Embark Studios) Key deets ⚡ You'll need Arc Performance Steel, Pop Trigger, Arc Thermo Lining, and Arc Synthetic Resin. ⚡Scan a crashed probe and courier then repair the Gondola Protoype east of the east Spaceport elevator and activate it. Arc Raiders ' To the Skies quest involves finding a few arc parts to repair one of the Prototype Gondolas being used to shuttle raiders to Pendola Pass. First things first, to complete To the Skies you're going to need a variety of arc parts: 1x Arc Performance Steel : Salvaged from big arcs like Bastions, Bombardiers, Leapers, or Baron Husks. 1x Pop Trigger : Salvaged from small exploding Pop robots or couriers. 1x Arc Thermo Lining : Salvaged from Pops, Fireballs, or Baron Husks. 1x Arc Synthetic Resin : Salvaged from intact Arc Probes or Baron Husks. There are a number of other ways to get the materials above, generally by salvaging arc enemies, so if you don't have one of each yet, keep your eyes peeled. title: Intel to release new CPUs on old socket in early 2027 says Gigabyte - memory crisis making DDR4 desirable again
summary: Likely to offer new options with DDR4 support.
body: Gigabyte is readying its B760 and H610 motherboards for new LGA1700 processors. Wait, what year is it? "Built on socket LGA1700 and expected to launch in early 2027," Gigabyte says in a post on its website, "the new processors bring fresh performance to an established platform, and Gigabyte users can be ready from day one." These are new LGA1700 chips. We're talking about fresh spins on Raptor Lake and Alder Lake here, which previously made up the 12th/13th/14th Gen, and were last released as a major launch in 2023 . That's a long time ago in CPU land. We've had two consecutive launches since, in Arrow Lake and the Arrow Lake refresh, neither of which dented AMD's stranglehold on the enthusiast market with its X3D chips. So what chance do these old chips have of selling anything? Quite a good one, actually, as these old chips still support DDR4 memory. DDR4 memory is currently a lot cheaper than DDR5 memory. We've seen big price hikes on both, but you can grab a DDR4-3600 32 GB kit for around $210 and a DDR5-6000 32 GB kit for $480 . Ouch. Back in August, Intel VP and GM for enthusiast channel, Robert Hallock, confirmed that Raptor Lake chips would stick around in Intel's portfoli…

title: Peter Molyneux explains the origin story of Black & White's famous creatures: 'It was originally a monster. It wasn't a cute creature'
summary: The father of the god game genre reveals all
body: Recently, I travelled to Guildford to interview Peter Molyneux, the father of the god game genre, about his final game, Masters of Albion , which just got a major, game-changing update . I've been a long-term fan of Molyneux's games, though, stretching all the way back to Theme Park, so I also took this opportunity to also ask the legendary game dev about, arguably, his most famous god game creation to date, Black & White . And, specifically, I wanted to know where the origin of Black & White's most famous creations came from: the titanic animal creatures that you, as god, nurture in the game and use as an instrument of your will. And, well, the story of how these creatures came to be is interesting. (Image credit: Lionhead Studios) Is Masters of Albion going to get titanic creatures? Molyneux's core strength, to me at least, has always been his uncontainable and seemingly endless creativity. The ability to dream up new games and features has led the legendary dev to create some of PC gaming's most iconic titles, including Populous, Theme Park, Dungeon Keeper, Black & White, and Fable. Yes, sure, implementing all those ideas perfectly has been a recurring challenge, but it's great…
